cards.title: The culture surrounding 'ideal' childbirth has to evolve
cards.body: Letters respond to an article about a five-day labour, with an NHS doctor sharing her experience of feeling 'othered' during childbirth. The discussion highlights how cultural expectations around 'ideal' birth experiences need to change.

cards.title: Parenting is hard. Should we let AI do it for us?
cards.body: Tech companies offer eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts and 'optimized nap predictions' for parents. The article questions whether parents actually need these AI-driven parenting tools.

cards.title: Should I try the '18 summers' parenting trend?
cards.body: The trend turns summer holidays into structured 'making memories' exercises rather than unscheduled downtime. Critics argue this controlling approach misses the point of childhood summers.

cards.title: Why your 'teachable moments' keep backfiring
cards.body: Explaining what went wrong while it's 'still fresh' feels like good parenting but is actually one of the most common ways parents accidentally create intense conflict. Timing and approach matter significantly.

cards.title: Why are gifted children, teenagers, and adults so intense?
cards.body: Gifted individuals often display heightened emotional intensity and sensitivity that can be misunderstood. Understanding their particular way of navigating the world is the first step toward supporting them.

cards.title: Neuroscience of asynchronous development in the bright mind
cards.body: Bright children often develop unevenly, with advanced abilities in some areas and age-typical skills in others. Parents simply need to pay closer attention to their child's particular ways of navigating the world.

cards.title: Stop bankrolling your adult child's stuck life
cards.body: Every financial bailout sends a message to your adult child—rarely the one you intended. Breaking the pattern helps them develop independence and resilience.
